newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end down on profit-taking, protest.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end down on profit-taking, protest.

text.p: Jakarta share prices ended lower in late trading on Thursday amid profit-taking in selected big-caps as an opposition political protest in the capital dampened sentiment, brokers said.
The composite index ended down 1.13 points, or 0.18 percent, at 628.32 points after hitting a high of 631.13 points earlier. Losers led gainers by 63 to 43, with 167 counters unchanged.
"Speculative buying of small-cap stocks helped limit the index's fall amid profit-taking in some blue-chips and soft sentiment following the demonstration," one local broker said.

Brokers said the market was cautious over any potential tension during the demonstration on Thursday by hundreds of supporters of ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri. The protest passed without incident.
The protest was the first organised opposition political demonstration in Jakarta since July when the capital was rocked by the worst riots in 20 years.
Brokers said big-capitalised Indosat, Citra Marga and Tambang Timah were among the losers on profit-taking.
They said, however, speculative buying of some small-capitalised stocks remained strong despite the protest.

Secondaries footwear manufacturer Telagamas, tyre-cord manufacturer Branta Mulia and food seasoning manufacturer Miwon were among the gainers following speculative buying due to a variety of market talk ranging from possible link-ups to acquisitions, they said.

About 300 supporters of Megawati passed petitions in parliament and national police headquarters to protest against the lack of action against a politician who ousted her as leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party.
